Cascaded linear gains multiply, rather than add.

questions.title: Practical: electrical cell counting
questions.subject: biophysics
questions.prompt: Why dilute a suspension for electrical counting?

options.text: To make each cell's true volume zero
options.explanation: Dilution changes concentration, not valid cell volume to zero.

options.text: To guarantee every event is a particular leukocyte type
options.explanation: Dilution does not establish cell identity.

options.text: To reduce simultaneous particles in the sensing aperture
options.explanation: Reduced concentration lowers coincidence probability under suitable counting conditions.

questions.title: Practical: diffusion slopes and uncertainty
questions.subject: biophysics
questions.prompt: Time increases ninefold at fixed D. RMS diffusion distance…

options.explanation: √9 = 3 gives a threefold distance scale.
RMS distance follows the square root of time.
Longer diffusion time increases the displacement scale.

questions.title: Practical: sound levels and audiograms
questions.subject: biophysics
questions.prompt: RMS sound pressure doubles under comparable conditions. SPL rises by approximately…

options.explanation: A factor of ten in pressure gives 20 dB.
20 log₁₀2 ≈ 6.02 dB.
About 3 dB corresponds to doubled intensity, not doubled pressure.

questions.prompt: Which circuit has one stable state and returns after a triggered pulse?

options.explanation: A bistable has two stable states.
An astable oscillates rather than resting in one stable state.
A monostable temporarily leaves its single stable state after a trigger.
